subject: Post-demo: data handling, subprocessors, and DPA clarifications
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Torres <samuel.torres@fincraft.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-09-30T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo recap + follow-up on data handling questions

Hi Samuel / Elena —

Thanks again for taking the demo this morning. Quick recap and a few clarifying notes you asked for so Legal/Engineering have something to review:

- Summary: Redwood is happy to support the FinCraft pilot for invoice parsing and categorization. The demo showed ingestion through the secure S3 connector and live inference via our Hosted API.
- Primary asks you had: controller/processor roles in the DPA, subprocessors list and notification window, log retention and access controls, and data residency options.

I put together a short summary and attached a dataflow diagram and a DPA summary PDF (see attachments). Highlights below — happy to run through on a call with your legal/infra folks.

Controller vs. Processor
- By default, FinCraft (you) is the Controller for customer-provided data and policy decisions; Redwood operates as Processor for data we process on your behalf.
- We do not assert ownership of your raw customer data.

Subprocessors
- Primary subprocessors used for pilot: AWS (EC2, S3), FastCache Inc. (KV cache), and TelemetryCo (aggregated usage analytics).
- We can provide a subprocessors list and a standard notification cadence. Our usual notice for new subprocessors is 30 days; for pilot customers we can discuss contractually shorter notice or an approval flow.

Retention and logs
- Default request logs and audit trails: retained 90 days (configurable).
- KV cache (model context) is ephemeral and configurable; default eviction is 24 hours but can be set to <1 hour for sensitive workloads.
- Access logs (who queried what) stored for 90 days; we offer extended retention as an add-on.

Breach notice
- Our standard DPA language: we notify Controllers without undue delay and provide details as we have them. For critical incidents we target 48–72 hours for initial notification depending on severity and investigation scope.

Next steps
1) I attached the DPA summary for your legal team.
2) If you’d like, schedule a 30-minute legal/infra sync — Ben (cc’d) can join for technical details on logging and residency.

Thanks — I’ll wait to hear what timeframe works best.

Best,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
phone: (415) 555-0132

Attachments: Redwood_DPA-summary_v1.pdf; PII-dataflow-diagram.png
From: Samuel Torres <samuel.torres@fincraft.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Martinez <elena.m@fincraft.ai>
Date: 2027-09-30T13:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + follow-up on data handling questions

Irene — thanks for the quick recap and attachments. A few clarifying Qs from Legal/Infra after scanning the summary: 

1) Controller/Processor boundary: Our legal team wants explicit examples in writing where Redwood would be considered a Controller (if any). For instance, any analytics-derived outputs that might include inferred PII — would Redwood ever treat that as separate personal data?

2) Subprocessor notification: 30 days is okay but our procurement team prefers an approval window for high-risk subprocessors (e.g., if you add a vendor that processes raw customer documents). Would a 14-day notice + right to object be possible?

3) Breach notice timing: The DPA phrase 'without undue delay' is vague for our SOC team. Do you have SLAs for initial notification (e.g., 48 hours) and a follow-up with root cause within 10 business days?

4) Logs & retention: We need a minimum of 12 months of tamper-evident access logs for audit purposes (one of our regulators requires this). Is extended retention + WORM-style log export possible?

5) Data residency: We’re in the process of choosing a pilot region; can you confirm availability of EU in-region hosting and whether model weights/derivatives ever leave region?

If possible, could you send a short redlineable DPA excerpt for these clauses so our legal team can accelerate?

Appreciate it. Can we get a legal/infra sync on Friday morning (PST)? Elena will coordinate.

—Sam
Head of Infra, FinCraft
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Samuel Torres <samuel.torres@fincraft.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + follow-up on data handling questions

Sam / Elena — thanks, great questions. Answers below and note on attachments: I added a SOC2 stub and a short DPA excerpt you can share internally.

1) Controller/Processor boundary
- Short answer: Redwood does not act as Controller for customer data collected and provided by FinCraft.
- Exception: if a customer explicitly asks Redwood to perform a processing activity where Redwood independently determines purposes and means (rare professional services engagement), we would document that in the contract. For typical inference and storage workflows, you remain the Controller.

2) Subprocessor notification / approval
- We can offer a 14-day notice window for high-risk subprocessors with an objection right for enterprise agreements (we’d map this to an approval flow in the Dedicated/Private offering). For Hosted pilots, we typically apply a notification + 7-day objection window; for your use case we can contractually set 14 days.

3) Breach notice SLA
- Initial notification: 48 hours for confirmed incidents affecting confidentiality/integrity where we can reasonably determine scope.
- Interim status updates: within 5 business days.
- Root cause/final report: target 15 business days; expedited if mutually agreed.

4) Logs & retention
- Extended retention available: we can export WORM-style access logs to your S3 bucket with 12-month retention. That export can be scheduled daily and is tamper-evident (signed manifests). This is part of our audit add-on.

5) Data residency
- EU in-region hosting: available in our EU cluster (Frankfurt and Dublin). Model weights are open-model artifacts and do not contain customer PII; however, runtime derivatives (cached contexts) can be pinned to region for Dedicated/Private deployments. For Hosted, we guarantee that customer data processed under EU tenancy remains in EU (we can provide residency attestations).

Next steps I propose:
- I’ve attached a DPA excerpt that includes the 14-day subprocessor notice + objection clause and the 48-hour initial notification SLA.
- Ben can run through the log export and WORM flow. Ben — can you confirm export format and S3 integration details (cc’d)?

If that looks good, let’s set the Friday legal/infra sync. Elena — if you can propose 0900–1100 PST windows, I’ll pick one.

Thanks,
Irene
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: SOC2-Report-stub.txt; Redwood_DPA-excerpt_14day-48hr.docx

- Infra confirms the WORM export approach sounds workable — they want the export manifest schema and S3 bucket lifecycle guidance. Ben, can you bring a sample manifest to the call?

Elena will send an invite for Friday 09:30 PST with Legal + Infra. Looking forward to the sync.
